root_cause.text: The mux/mmio driver’s probe path allocated an MMIO regmap with the non-device-managed `regmap_init_mmio()` and never released it on probe failure or driver removal, causing a resource leak in `mux_mmio_probe()`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “The mmio regmap that may be allocated during probe is never freed” and the patch fixes this by replacing `regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)` with `devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)`, explicitly to ensure cleanup on “probe failures (e.g. probe deferral) and on driver unbind.”

intent_record.what: The probe function changes the MMIO regmap creation call from regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg) to devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg), leaving the surrounding error handling and fallback logic unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the regmap allocated for the device becomes device-managed and will be automatically released when the device is detached or probe cleanup occurs, preventing manual resource lifetime issues such as leaks while preserving the same probing and error-path behavior.
